Definition: One row of a schedule: which intervention, for whom, when, how many doses. This is the granularity a decision table actually consumes — the BCG rules turn on dose count, age and interval since a live vaccine. Class IRI: http://smart.who.int/kg/schedule-entry.
The antigen or vaccine the row is about.
Dose in the series as printed ("1", "Booster 1"). Text, because schedules label boosters rather than count them.
Primary series or booster series, as stated.
Age at which the dose is due, as stated.
Minimum interval since the previous dose, as stated.
The row's footnote or remark, verbatim.
